Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed Redwood internally and have two gating requirements before Procurement will sign the MAP:

1) Regional routing SLA: We need the ability to ensure latency targets for our EU/US traffic by routing inference requests to a specific region (pinning by customer tenant or token). Required 99th percentile latency 400ms for standard prompts (up to 1024 tokens).

2) Audit-log export: Compliance needs an automated daily export of all request/response metadata (including prompts, token counts, timestamps, model variant) to our S3 bucket with HMAC integrity checks. Retention policy 1 year.

Attached is a short security questionnaire and the draft Mutual Action Plan (FinServe_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx).

We can move quickly if Redwood can commit to a timeline and a limited-scope delivery plan (prototype + canary). Procurement prefers an initial 6-month reserved commit with option to expand.

Please loop in Product/Eng — we are aiming to sign in the next 4–6 weeks.

Thanks for the heads-up, Marissa. Short product read here after a quick triage meeting with Eng/Privacy:

Clarifying Qs for Priya (copying here so you can decide if you want to respond directly):
- For regional routing, do you require hard per-tenant region enforcement (requests never leave the selected region) or soft preference with failover?
- For audit logs, does FinServe require full prompt/response bodies encrypted at rest in their S3, or are metadata-only exports acceptable initially?
- Expected qps/peaks and retention beyond 1 year?

Proposed prioritization options (tradeoffs):
A) High-priority MVP (recommended if legal/procurement can accept scope limits):
   - Tenant-scoped routing flag + routing policy (US/EU) with a canary toggle — prototype in ~3–4 weeks (spike + basic UI + routing tag).
   - Audit log export: metadata-only daily export (timestamp, request_id, model_variant, token_counts) to their S3 with HMAC; prototype in ~3–6 weeks (depending on security review).
   - Risks: performance SLO unknown at scale; per-tenant routing increases cache fragmentation and could increase cost.

B) Full compliance delivery (GA): 8–12 weeks — includes hard region isolation, encrypted full-body export, KMS integration, formal security review, and SLA testing.

We can support an accelerated spike if Sales secures explicit pre-commit (deposit or signed MAP) to allocate an eng sprint and a security reviewer slot. If Finance/Legal need an exception to our normal SLA matrix, please capture it in the MAP.

If you want, I can draft the scoped MVP spec and acceptance criteria by end of week. Needs Eng confirmation on effort.

—Aisha
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — a quick technical read from Eng:

TL;DR: Scoped MVP possible with an engineering spike (~4 weeks) to validate routing tag flow + S3 export of metadata. Full GA (hard isolation + encrypted bodies + KMS integration) ~10–12 weeks.

Notes/constraints:
- Per-tenant hard region enforcement requires changes in routing layer and our placement policy; current runtime assumes global KV cache that benefits cross-region hits. Hard isolation will fragment caches and likely increase tail latency and cost per token.
- We can implement a per-tenant routing flag that pins new sessions to a region and introduces a regional cache partitioning; POC 3–4 weeks but will need a scoped load test to validate 99p latency.
- Audit log export: metadata pipeline is straightforward (we already emit request metadata to internal event bus). Building an S3 sink with HMAC + customer-provided bucket access is ~2–3 weeks once security signs off. Full bodies require additional privacy review and storage encryption controls.
- Dependencies: Security review (privacy + retention), infra capacity (we'll need a named canary cluster), and product acceptance criteria. Also need an ops playbook for incident handling for tenant-isolated routing.

Proposal (what Eng can deliver if Sales secures a pre-commit):
1) 2-week discovery + spike (routing tag + minimal S3 sink) — outcome: working canary and list of perf regressions.
2) 2-week implement canary and automated daily export for metadata only.
3) 4–6 week follow-up for full compliance items (KMS, encrypted bodies, SLA testing).

If we start discovery next Monday and Sales confirms fund/commit, we can have a canary by the end of April. Otherwise GA still likely in June.

-Jordan
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
